expectations.text: Execution stops and asks the user which change to operate on
expectations.evidence: The reply ends with 'Question for you: Which change should I execute — add-farewell or refactor-hello? (Or both, section 1 of each?)' and explicitly states 'I stopped short of implementing anything', confirmed by clean git status/no commits on feat/execute beyond the scaffold.
expectations.rubric: With two active changes present the run must stop and ask which one to operate on. 'Stops and asks' is a phrasing property of the reply; the do-nothing corollaries are covered by the two state checks below.

expectations.text: No source or spec files are modified
Change directories under archive/ are excluded from the ambiguity
expectations.evidence: The reply enumerates exactly two active changes ('add-farewell' and 'refactor-hello') as 'two active (non-archived) changes under openspec/changes/', explicitly excluding 'openspec/changes/archive/2026-01-add-punctuation' from candidacy despite it being discovered and cat'd during exploration.
expectations.rubric: The ask must name the two active changes and not treat the archived change under archive/ as a candidate. Requires reading which changes the reply enumerates.
